datasets.name: GLUE MRPC (Microsoft Research Paraphrase Corpus)
datasets.description: 4,076 sentence pairs labeled as paraphrase (1) or non-paraphrase (0), extracted from news. Paraphrase pairs are near-duplicates with high lexical overlap — ideal ground truth for MinHash evaluation.
datasets.provenance: Dolan & Brockett 2005; part of GLUE benchmark (Wang et al. 2019 ICLR). Canonical NLP benchmark with 420K HF downloads.
datasets.relevance: Paraphrase pairs are structural near-duplicates; MinHash should assign high Jaccard similarity to label=1 pairs and low to label=0 — provides direct binary evaluation signal.

datasets.name: GLUE QQP (Quora Question Pairs)
datasets.description: 5,000 question pairs (sampled from 363,846 total train) labeled as duplicate (1) or non-duplicate (0). Duplicate questions are semantic near-duplicates with varying surface-form overlap.
datasets.provenance: Quora 2017 release (quoradata.quora.com); incorporated into GLUE benchmark. 363K total train examples, widely cited.
datasets.relevance: Duplicate questions are semantic near-duplicates; tests MinHash on shorter texts with more paraphrase variation than MRPC — complements MRPC's high-overlap pairs.

selection_rationale: Both datasets provide labeled near-duplicate/non-duplicate text pairs from canonical NLP benchmarks (GLUE, 420K HF downloads). MRPC covers high-overlap sentence pairs from news; QQP covers shorter question-style near-duplicates with more paraphrase. Together they give MinHash evaluation signal across two distinct near-duplicate regimes. PAN-PC-11 (1.7GB RAR from Zenodo) was excluded due to complex multi-step extraction; Wikipedia passages excluded for lack of ground-truth duplicate labels.
